items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I sent to Washington and I got a bass player Fred Williams, and a drummer, Harold Chavis. I think we had a couple of weeks there in Chicago which proved to be pretty nice.

ctx.x: Anyway, after that, I flew back to Washington, and I started working in a club that was owned by a fellow named Pete Lambros, but the main attraction there was a guitarist whose name was Charlie Byrd. I worked up there for I guess the better part of two years. But while I was there, I did some other miscellaneous engagements with people, one of them being Joe Williams. I did a thing, I was back in California again with him. We were there for something like two or three weeks.

After that we did a club in Chicago, called I think Basin Street. I had a trio there, I believe... Yeah, I sent to Washington and I got a bass player Fred Williams, and a drummer, Harold Chavis. I think we had a couple of weeks there in Chicago which proved to be pretty nice.

After that... I guess this is about up to 1965. Since then, everything has been pretty much around Washington, D.C. There have been groups and there have been trios, and a lot of things that I've done here with the better musicians around Washington.
